title: Respiratory hygiene, cough etiquette and waiting areas
audience: Cleaning and support workers who clean waiting areas, reception points and entrances in healthcare settings.
learningOutcomes: Demonstrate the cough etiquette steps for a person with respiratory symptoms.
Name four items a facility should supply for respiratory hygiene.
Describe how spacing and signage in a waiting area reduce spread.

instruction.heading: Why coughs and sneezes matter
instruction.body: Respiratory infections such as influenza and COVID-19 spread through the droplets released when people cough or sneeze. Cough etiquette aims to stop those droplets reaching other people and surfaces. The guide expects everyone with symptoms of a respiratory infection to follow it, and that includes staff, visitors and clients.

instruction.heading: Cover, bin, clean
instruction.body: When you cough or sneeze, shield your nose and mouth with a paper tissue or the crook of your elbow when no tissue is to hand. Put a used tissue straight into the nearest bin, never into a pocket. Then clean your hands using soap and water, or hand rub, following the method in “Hand cleaning: when to do it and which product fits”. The guide specifies ordinary, non-antimicrobial soap for this step, so check which soap your facility supplies.

instruction.heading: Supplies and layout a facility should provide
instruction.body: The guide expects waiting and public areas to hold tissues and a no-touch bin for used tissues. Hand-rub dispensers, which contain alcohol, should be placed where people actually need them, such as the doorway of a ward or next to a bed. Every sink should have soap and single-use paper towels. Posters and visual signs in the languages visitors use should be placed by area doorways as reminders. The guide also suggests asking visitors to report any airway infection on arrival, so that staff can help them practise cough etiquette. Anyone who is coughing should sit away from other people in the waiting room.

instruction.heading: Your role as the cleaner
instruction.body: You top up tissues and bins and report empty dispensers and missing soap or towels straight away, because staff and visitors depend on them. You clean the high-contact points in a waiting area on the schedule (see “Cleaning sequence, routine cleaning and checklists”). You do not remove or cover signs. If a person is coughing, you do not confront them. You point them to the tissues and the hand rub and tell the reception or the nurse, who will manage the situation.

procedure: Check each waiting area for tissues, a no-touch bin, hand rub and, at sinks, soap and paper towels.
Top up supplies from stock, or report an empty dispenser to the supervisor straight away.
If a person is coughing, do not confront them. Point them to tissues and hand rub, and tell reception or the nurse.
Clean your own hands after handling tissues, bins or the dispenser.
Record stock shortages and dispenser faults with the location and the time.

workedExamples.situation: A visitor sneezes into their hands in a waiting room and then touches the sign-in screen.
workedExamples.decisionPrompt: What happens to the screen and to the visitor?
workedExamples.reasoning: Clean the touched surface with the approved product on the schedule, and clean your own hands after. Ask the visitor to use the hand rub, and tell reception so they can check whether the visitor has symptoms and needs a nurse.

workedExamples.situation: A cleaner finds the hand rub dispenser empty at a ward entrance.
workedExamples.reasoning: Report it to the supervisor straight away, because staff and visitors rely on it. Do not swap in a different product without approval, because that may not suit the setting.

equipmentAndPpe: Disposable gloves for cleaning touched surfaces
Tissues, no-touch bin and hand rub stock for top-up
Approved product for the surface being cleaned

commonErrors.error: Keeping used tissues in a pocket or on a bench until later.
commonErrors.prevention: Put each used tissue straight into the nearest bin.

commonErrors.error: Covering a cough with a bare hand and then touching a door or handrail.
commonErrors.prevention: Clean your hands, then clean the surfaces you touched.

commonErrors.error: Removing or covering a sign because it looks untidy.
commonErrors.prevention: Report a damaged or missing sign and leave the sign in place.

safetyAndRegulatory.point: Do not refuse entry or ask a visitor or client to leave. Refer the matter to reception or the nurse in charge.

qualityStandard: Learner demonstrates the three cough etiquette steps in order, with the hand clean as the final step.
Learner names four items a facility should provide for respiratory hygiene.
Learner explains why a coughing person is seated apart and why the sign is left in place.
documentationEvidence: Stock top-up record or dispenser fault report with location and time.
summary: Cover the cough, bin the tissue, then clean the hands.
A facility should supply tissues, a no-touch bin, hand rub and soap at each sink.
Report empty dispensers and damaged signs rather than replacing them yourself.

knowledgeChecks.question: A person coughs. Which is the correct cough etiquette step?
options: Cough into the palm, then wipe the hand on the uniform
Cover the nose and mouth with tissue or the crook of the elbow
Cough into a cupped hand onto a bench and then wipe it with a hand towel
Turn away and cough onto the floor and then carry on with the task

knowledgeChecks.question: Which item belongs in the respiratory hygiene supplies a facility should provide?
options: Reusable cotton hand towels for every room
Tissues and a bin operated without hands
A shared cup for drinks at the front desk
Open bins with no lids beside the front desk

knowledgeChecks.question: What is the main purpose of seating a coughing person apart from others in a waiting area?
options: To avoid the cost of extra chairs in the waiting area
To reduce how easily droplets from the cough reach others
To stop people from talking to each other in the waiting area
To make waiting times longer for everyone in the clinic
